headline: Energy Leads, Homebuilders Lag as Markets Close Out July on a Split Note
body_html:
Equities ended Friday's session in modest positive territory on balance, with 273 names advancing against 246 declining across a 519-stock universe — a narrow but real tilt to the bulls to close out July. Energy stood out as the clear sector winner, rising 1.64%, while Software added 0.89% and Industrials contributed 0.71%. Semiconductors eked out a 0.31% gain, suggesting appetite for growth names remained cautious rather than conviction-driven heading into the weekend.

The damage was concentrated in Homebuilders, which surrendered 1.72%, and Healthcare, off 0.97%, while Consumer names slipped 0.89%. The session's most dramatic single-stock moves came from earnings-driven swings: DexCom surged 11.95% and SPS Commerce jumped 11.48% on well-received results, while Roblox cratered 26.85% and Veracyte tumbled 22.52% on disappointments. Infrastructure contractor MasTec fell 18.91% and GoDaddy shed 16.70%, adding to the session's volatility.

The week ahead arrives with geopolitical tension elevated — the White House convened a Cabinet meeting at Camp David amid renewed Iran-related pressure — and investors will be watching whether the S&P 500 can break free of a contested technical level that has capped progress. Microsoft's recent strength and Amazon management's effort to reassure on AI capital expenditure set a constructive backdrop for mega-cap tech, but the tape will require broader participation to sustain any meaningful advance.

briefs.headline: Amazon Leadership Moves to Calm AI Spending Anxiety
briefs.body: Amazon's chief executive took deliberate steps over the weekend to address investor unease surrounding the company's elevated artificial-intelligence capital outlays, offering a framework for how that spending translates to competitive returns. The reassurance arrives as the broader market scrutinizes whether AI infrastructure investment cycles are approaching a point of diminishing near-term payoff.

briefs.headline: Eaton Climbs as Industrials Attract Dip-Buyers
briefs.body: Eaton rose 7.32% on Friday, helping the Industrials sector post a 0.71% gain and drawing attention from commentators who flagged the electrical-equipment maker as a buying opportunity for those without existing exposure. The move underscores renewed interest in power-infrastructure plays as electrification themes reassert themselves.

briefs.headline: Databricks Pre-IPO Access Opens to Broader Investor Base
briefs.body: Fintech brokerage Clear Street announced it is giving clients the ability to take positions in Databricks ahead of a potential public offering, with the data-and-AI platform carrying a reported valuation of $188 billion. The move reflects growing demand for pre-IPO allocation channels as marquee private technology names delay traditional listings.

briefs.headline: Roblox Suffers Its Steepest Single-Session Drop in Recent Memory
briefs.body: Shares of Roblox plunged 26.85% on Friday, making it the worst performer in the universe after the gaming and social platform delivered results that fell short of expectations. The collapse dragged on the broader Internet-Gaming category and raised fresh questions about monetisation trajectories for user-generated-content platforms.

briefs.headline: New York Regulators Take Aim at Prediction Market Kalshi
briefs.body: New York State filed suit against prediction-market operator Kalshi, alleging the platform is conducting an unlicensed gambling operation within state borders. The legal challenge marks one of the most significant regulatory confrontations yet for the fast-growing prediction-market industry and could shape federal and state oversight debates heading into autumn.

briefs.headline: GM Prepares In-Vehicle AI Launch for Later This Year
briefs.body: General Motors disclosed plans to introduce a new artificial-intelligence system embedded directly in its vehicles before year-end, intensifying competition in automotive AI as the sector races to differentiate on software capability. The announcement adds momentum to an emerging battleground that increasingly influences consumer purchase decisions and long-term platform revenue.
